task.source: method of Jones, Scaling Scaling Laws with Board Games (arXiv:2104.03113), on a 13x13 board (the paper stops at 9x9, which research sessions saturated)
task.board: 13x13 rhombus of hexagonal cells, cell = 13*row + col
task.first_player: black, joins top and bottom edges
task.second_player: white, joins left and right edges
task.termination: natural connection; no draws; at most 169 moves
task.observation: full board int8[169], side to move, legal mask bool[169]
task.engine: frozen batched PyTorch engine (GPU and CPU), checked against an independent BFS reference

resources.practice_worker: 8 CPU cores, 16 GiB, no GPU; charged to the research budget at its shape's rate
resources.leases: 0 or 1 L40S, 1-32 CPU cores, 2-64 GiB, researcher commands, shared /scratch Volume
resources.concurrency: seconds mode: one active job (a run, a practice or a lease); usd mode: 4 active jobs, at most 2 with a GPU and 64 CPU cores in total
resources.charging: seconds mode: training-worker seconds = worker seconds x cost(shape) / cost(training worker); usd mode: US dollars = worker seconds x cost(shape); cost at the frozen Modal sandbox list prices in contract.py PRICE

usd_mode.concurrency: parallel: up to 4 jobs, 2 GPUs, 64 CPU cores

starter.algorithm: REINFORCE with a learned value baseline and entropy bonus; Adam; pure self-play; greedy at evaluation

architecture.input: canonical 2x13x13 planes from the side to move

evaluation.openings: 2-ply (black cell, white cell), drawn without replacement from all 28392
evaluation.seats: every opening played twice, candidate as black and as white
evaluation.panel_calibration: reports/hex/panel-calibration-13x13-2026-11-14.json; epsilon = chance of a uniformly random move
evaluation.anchor: MoHex 2.0 (benzene-vanilla-cmake), parallel DFPN solver, knowledge threshold 0, 50000 games per move; a strong reference on 13x13, not perfect play
evaluation.secondary: candidate Elo fitted against the calibrated panel; Elo against the anchor alone; per-seat and per-opponent win rates; the campaign head-to-head tournament
evaluation.reference_normalized: null: the raw score is anchored on MoHex and needs no calibration run
evaluation.move_clock: a policy call covering n positions (n <= inference_batch) must answer within call_seconds + n * position_seconds of wall time on one CPU thread
evaluation.late_moves: a policy call answered after its move clock is replaced by uniformly random legal moves for every game in it
evaluation.faults: no ordinary score for an illegal or malformed policy answer, a policy that does not load, a MoHex fault or an incomplete schedule
evaluation.tournament: every campaign ends with a round robin of its final networks plus the five strongest panel opponents (tools/hex_tournament.py), under the same move clock

commands.smoke: .venv-hex/bin/python -m harness run hex network --release RELEASE --out SESSION --smoke --model MODEL --execute
